lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.

The federal government on Friday prioritized construction of a critical road in the Northwest Territories by designating the Mackenzie Valley Highway as a project of national interest, The Canadian Press reports.

The Supreme Court of Canada has upheld Quebec’s secularism law and its use of the notwithstanding clause – as Saskatchewan waits to have its own case heard in the new year, The Canadian Press reports.
Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is heading to Washington next week as trade talks between Canada and the United States continue, The Canadian Press reports.
The CRTC issued a ruling Friday saying that carriers violated its prohibition on charging a fee for providing and setting up cellphones when signing up for a service plan, The Canadian Press reports.

The federal government says seven teams have been selected to take part in a design competition to restore the prime minister’s official residence at 24 Sussex Drive in Ottawa, The Canadian Press reports.
Heavy rain winds down as power remains out for hundreds of thousands on the U.S. East Coast, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
